subject: LAB-013
check: SpeechTimelinePhoneTests and SpeechTimelinePhoneQualificationTests pass across eight targeted iOS app test runs after the Focus-context launch fix
inputs: Focus selection: one lab-alert identifier, foreign.alert, and an empty selection (original synthetic inputs)
steps: LAB_SIMULATOR_PREFIX="NL LAB-013-B" script/qualify_speech_timeline_phone.sh on the build host
Create one ticket-owned iPhone simulator; build and test once, then test-without-building seven times
Read each xcresult summary and require Passed, 3 passed tests and 0 failed tests; never accept an empty selection
Delete the simulator created for the run in the EXIT trap

outcome.detail: Eight of eight targeted runs passed, each with 3 passed, 0 failed, and 0 skipped tests: 24 passing executions. The real Focus context constructed and evaluated the allowed, foreign and empty selections. The device voice synthesized the original sample; SpeechTranscriber reported unavailable and the flow returned its stated failure. The host session imported 4 captions, corrected without moving timestamps, annotated, exported, saved through an app-UI receipt, refused recording before capture, and reset while preserving the saved transcript. No runner reported Crash: NativeLab. These are repeated simulator checks, not device recognition or a statistical reliability guarantee.

limitations: iOS 27.0 simulator only; the transcriber is unavailable, so these runs prove the unavailable route and the caption fallback, not recognition on an iPhone.
No microphone, model download, physical iPhone or iPad, notification delivery, or person enabling a Focus was exercised.

One simulator was reused across eight app test runs; per-test stores and temporary audio folders were fresh and removed by the tests. No clean-install matrix or explicit synthetic CPU-load generator was used.
The two other selected tests execute alongside the synthesis test using Swift Testing scheduling. Research was shared and queued; system load was not measured.
Raw result summaries and result bundles stay in build; committed evidence omits simulator identifiers and machine paths.
